#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This restarts the init container if it is stuck in the created state, as it may have failed to start correctly.
This fixes a regression from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116429.

issue_context.title: `SyncPod` may fail to start a pod with init container if `RunContainerError` occurs and SidecarContainers is enabled
comments:
/sig node

@gjkim42, @matthyx, @SergeyKanzhelev can you help checking this issue report as according to @Kostov6 it is a regression introduced with https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116429? Thanks in advance!

I guess this is a valid bug.
/triage accepted
/priority important-soon

@Kostov6 
Can you provide a more specific scenario for this?
Why do container runtime fail to start the container? (How can I reproduce it in e2e test?)

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/00236ae0d73d2455a2470469ed1005674f8ed61f/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/kuberuntime_container.go#L1085-L1087
^
I guess this is the wrong assumption.
If the container is in the `ContainerStateCreated` state, the kubelet should resync it.
During node bootstrapping we had a bug where `containerd` got restarted. So it is possible the following to happen: container gets created -> `containerd` restarts -> container fails to start

We have a similar case. I have not yet looked at how containerd behaves at the moment, because it happens rarely and only at node startup.
Pod stuck in the `CreateContainerError` status. In the suppress status we have the following message:

```

          is reserved for "6dd5ece479a0d540f86f8b4817fa299f92df99181b178a0b78dcae61b012d444"'
        reason: CreateContainerError
```

`worker-16x48-e55f5ba2-859c7-qfqkx   Ready    worker,worker-16x48    13h    v1.29.5   10.160.0.47     <none>        Ubuntu 22.04.2 LTS   5.15.0-76-generic   containerd://1.7.13`

And it's like the error is reproduced on 1.29. The neighbouring cluster with k8s 1.28 is not affected by this problem

we have observed a similar behaviour but intermittently while upgrading our k8s cluster from **k8s 1.29.0 to 1.29.6**.

During upgrade process, when the node gets rebooted the "calico-node" pod of that node got stuck with below error forever until i restart the pod manually. 

`pod_workers.go:1298] "Error syncing pod, skipping" err="failed to \"StartContainer\" for \"install-cni\" with RunContainerError: \"error reading from server: EOF\"" pod="kube-system/calico-node-bm4lt" podUID="b8966d56-e312-4c55-8c22-562bf96eb18d"`

Note: We are not observing this every time. Please let me know for any additional info required.

review_comments: I see, you're adding a test case here because the kubelet handles the Regular Containers [the same way](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/00236ae0d73d2455a2470469ed1005674f8ed61f/pkg/kubelet/container/helpers.go#L89-L92).

computeInitContainerActions looks like a new code path only enabled when the SidecarContainers feature is enabled?

taking a step back, should we only take this new code path in pods which actually have made use of the sidecar feature? ideally, bugs in this new code path would only impact pods that have specifically opted into using the new sidecar feature, and all other pods would have their behavior stay the same.
I would like to remove the old code path while updating the new one once the SidecarContainers feature reaches GA, since there is a lot of shared logic for the init container's actions.

> I would like to remove the old code path while updating the new one once the SidecarContainers feature reaches GA, since there is a lot of shared logic for the init container's actions.

The number one priority is to ensure that pods that didn't opt into the new feature are not impacted by bugs in the new code path. This is the second time the sidecar feature has regressed, so I think it's important to leave the old code path active for pods which have not opted in until the new code path has proven it works correctly over multiple releases.

I agree that it should have been implemented in that way, but it might be a bit late now since the sidecar wg is considering to promote this feature to GA in the next release...

cc @SergeyKanzhelev

> it might be a bit late now since the sidecar wg is considering to promote this feature to GA in the next release...

I do not agree. The presence of a regression in this code path should make us hesitant to make this code path unconditional yet. Recovering compatibility for 1.29-1.31 should be our top priority. Reviewing these changes and closing test gaps should be our second priority. Promotion to GA should come after all of those.
ok, I'll create a PR for that to minimize the impact of the new code path.
Can you explain why container considered stuck if it's in the `ContainerStateCreated` state?

That is because of the old code that does nothing in the Created state.
I'll rephrase it.

(done)

It still looks to me like we're trying to unconditionally restart container if it's in the `ContainerStateCreated` state. Where this state is set? Where is it updated? Why is it `likely that the container runtime has failed to start the container` if the container is in this state?

/hold
Should we check CreatedAt field and only restart a container after a certain timeout?

This is a part of the main sync loop and
1. it checks the state
2. calls the CreateContainer
3. calls the StartContainer

in sequence with blocking manner (waiting for the result).

Therefore, if a container is in the Created state at step 1, it means that the container runtime has failed to StartContainer.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126543/files#r1704785057
^
The regular containers behave in the same way as well.

Does it make sense?

It does. Thanks for the explanations!
/unhold

This can cause the same issue as #123087 for init containers when `EventedPLEG` is enabled.

Container statuses evaluated here are updated asynchronously by PLEG. So, `ContainerStateCreated` could be seen when a container is starting normally especially with `EventedPLEG` enabled.
xref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122778#issuecomment-1956910606

Thanks for sharing! I see that the change to prevent Regular containers from restarting in the Created state when Evented PLEG is enabled will be made in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122778.

This PR fixes a regression in Generic PLEG caused by Sidecar Containers feature. We could either merge this PR first and then address the case for initContainers in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122778, or we could take a different approach. Based on the  https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3386#issuecomment-2309247626, it looks like there might be some progress with https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122778 in near future too.

/cc @pacoxu

This addressed the problem of Generic PLEG. 

/lgtm
/approve

@gjkim42 if (and only if) you happen to resubmit, could you please add more of your comment https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/126543/commits/7e8ea57cc6ee29631e8a66cc521a48803a16cd14#r1724882374 in the code comment? I feel the github comment concisely and clearly describes the fix so it would be great to have it in the codebase and not lost in github review comments.
